# TCB Allowed List — Nanvix phys-mm

Any `external_body` outside this list must be removed.

## Allowed `external_body`

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_physical_memory_regions` — iterates a std
  `alloc::collections::LinkedList` via `for region in list.iter()`. The build
  toolchain's `vstd` (`/mnt/toolchain/verus/vstd`) ships ghost-iterator specs only
  for `slice`/`vec`/`VecDeque`/`BTree*`/`Hash*` iterators, **not** `LinkedList`, and
  the orphan rule forbids supplying `View`/`ForLoopGhostIterator` impls for the
  foreign `linked_list::Iter` from the `kernel` crate (E0117). Genuine Verus
  front-end limitation, not a proof gap or code bug — full analysis in
  `verus-unsupported.md`. The abstract booking effect is specified over
  `PhysMemView` and discharged (no `admit`) by
  `lemma_book_region_reserves_region_frames` in `mod.proof.rs`. `ensures` keeps the
  caller-relevant guarantee: allocator stays initialized and well-formed.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/mod.rs::book_mmio_regions` — same std-`LinkedList`
  iteration limitation as above. Abstract effect (skip-if-not-covered; book tracked
  frames) discharged by `lemma_book_mmio_skip_untracked` /
  `lemma_book_mmio_books_tracked`. `ensures` keeps allocator initialized and
  well-formed across booking.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::deref_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/kframe.rs::KernelFrame::clear`- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` — materializes a
  `&'static mut [u8; N]` from a backend-provided address (`usize as *mut`); raw-memory
  op Verus cannot verify without a `PointsTo` for the externally-owned `BssStorage`
  region. Mirrors `src/libs/raw-array`. `ensures` states alignment + in-bounds over
  the abstract `bump_view`.
- `src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs::FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc_as` — delegates to
  `alloc` and re-materializes the slot as `&'static mut MaybeUninit<T>`; same rationale.
  `ensures` adds the `size_of::<T>()`/`align_of::<T>()` vs `(N, A)` guard arms.

## Skip / exclude from current proof target

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::get_mut`
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::init`

## Allowed `external_body` — `frame::*` free-function shims (`frame.rs`)

The module-level `frame::*` free functions bridge the global allocator singleton
(`static mut INSTANCE`, reached via `instance()`) to the do-not-modify abstract
`phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView`. That bridge is a trust boundary identical in
character to the already-trusted `frame::book` / `frame::is_covered` /
`frame::alloc_range` shims: `phys_view()` is a zero-argument uninterpreted spec
function whose value cannot be tied to the `unsafe { INSTANCE.assume_init_mut() }`
static by any verifiable means. Each is `external_body` with a `#[verus_spec]`
contract stated over `phys_view()` and the returned frame values (monotone
post-state facts; there is no `old(phys_view())`). They were left unspecced when
`frame.rs` was the proof target because their sole consumer is `mm::phys::upool`;
they are specced here so `upool` can rely on them, and will be removed when the
frame singleton bridge is itself verified.

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::alloc` — draws a fresh frame from the global
  allocator. `ensures` (on success) page alignment, membership in
  `allocated_frames`, and refcount = 1.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::free` — releases one reference (last reference
  returns the frame to the free pool). Runs on `Drop`, so it has no precondition;
  `ensures` keeps the subsystem invariant on every path.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::share` — adds a reference to an allocated
  frame. `ensures` (on success) the frame stays allocated / refcounted.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/frame.rs::refcount` — pure query of an allocated frame's
  reference count. `ensures` (on success) the returned count equals the frame's
  refcount; (on failure) the frame is not allocated.

## Allowed `external_body` — `UserFrame::drop` (`upool.rs`)

`UserFrame::drop` releases the frame's reference by calling `frame::free` and, on
the error path, logs via the `error!` macro. The `error!`/`write!` expansion uses
`core::fmt` Debug formatting (`{:?}`), which Verus cannot translate to VIR
("Unsupported constant type"). The function is therefore `external_body`; its
`#[verus_spec]` contract is honored by trusting that body. The contract is not a
new guarantee — `ensures phys_view().inv()` is exactly the post-state already
established by the `external_body` `frame::free` shim it calls, and the logging
branch performs no state change. `opens_invariants none` / `no_unwind` record that
`drop` opens no invariant and cannot unwind (errors are logged, not propagated).

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/upool.rs::<UserFrame as Drop>::drop` — releases one
  reference on scope exit. `ensures phys_view().inv()` on every path.

## Allowed `external_body` — `PhysMemoryManager` (`manager.rs`)

`PhysMemoryManager` is a **stateless facade** over the global frame allocator
(`Upool` has no fields; kernel frames are drawn from the global `frame::*`
statics through `static mut PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER`). Its target methods therefore
have no verifiable body: they mutate global `static mut` state, call un-specced
upstream allocator primitives, and use side-effecting combinators
(`inspect_err`/`and_then`/`ok_or_else`) and `error!`/`warn!` macros that are not
ghost-gated and have no `vstd` specs. They form a trust boundary identical in
character to the `frame.rs` shims: each is `external_body` with a `#[verus_spec]`
contract stated over the do-not-modify `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView` and the
returned frame values (monotone post-state facts, as there is no
`old(phys_view())`). Abstract laws are carried by `manager.proof.rs` lemmas.

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::init` — writes the
  global `static mut PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER` (`MaybeUninit::write`) and flips an
  `AtomicBool`. `ensures` keeps the allocator initialized and well-formed.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::alloc_user_frame` —
  draws a frame from the global allocator and wraps it as a `UserFrame`.
  `ensures` (on success) places the returned frame's address in
  `allocated_frames` and states page alignment.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::check_user_watermark` —
  reads the build-time `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK` and the global free
  count. `ensures` (on success) gives `spec_watermark_ok` and keeps
  `free_frames` finite.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::alloc_many_user_frames`
  — loop-allocates `count` user frames into a caller `&mut Vec`, with all-or-
  nothing cleanup. `ensures` gives `len == count` and each frame allocated on
  success, empty vector on error.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::alloc_kernel_frame` —
  like `alloc_user_frame` but yields a `KernelFrame`.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::alloc_many_kernel_frames`
  — like `alloc_many_user_frames` plus the contiguity guarantee
  (`kernel_frames_contiguous`) required for kernel stacks.

`UserFrame::drop` releases the frame's reference by calling `frame::free` and, on
the error path, logs via the `error!` macro. The `error!`/`write!` expansion uses
`core::fmt` Debug formatting (`{:?}`), which Verus cannot translate to VIR
("Unsupported constant type"). The function is therefore `external_body`; its
`#[verus_spec]` contract is honored by trusting that body. The contract is not a
new guarantee — `ensures phys_view().inv()` is exactly the post-state already
established by the `external_body` `frame::free` shim it calls, and the logging
branch performs no state change. `opens_invariants none` / `no_unwind` record that
`drop` opens no invariant and cannot unwind (errors are logged, not propagated).

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/upool.rs::<UserFrame as Drop>::drop` — releases one
  reference on scope exit. `ensures phys_view().inv()` on every path.

## Allowed `external_body` — `PhysMemoryManager` (`manager.rs`)

`PhysMemoryManager` is a **stateless facade** over the global frame allocator
(`Upool` has no fields; kernel frames are drawn from the global `frame::*`
statics through `static mut PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER`). Its target methods therefore
have no verifiable body: they mutate global `static mut` state, call un-specced
upstream allocator primitives, and use side-effecting combinators
(`inspect_err`/`and_then`/`ok_or_else`) and `error!`/`warn!` macros that are not
ghost-gated and have no `vstd` specs. They form a trust boundary identical in
character to the `frame.rs` shims: each is `external_body` with a `#[verus_spec]`
contract stated over the do-not-modify `phys_view()` / `FrameAllocView` and the
returned frame values (monotone post-state facts, as there is no
`old(phys_view())`). Abstract laws are carried by `manager.proof.rs` lemmas.

- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::init` — writes the
  global `static mut PHYS_MEMORY_MANAGER` (`MaybeUninit::write`) and flips an
  `AtomicBool`. `ensures` keeps the allocator initialized and well-formed.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::alloc_user_frame` —
  draws a frame from the global allocator and wraps it as a `UserFrame`.
  `ensures` (on success) places the returned frame's address in
  `allocated_frames` and states page alignment.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::check_user_watermark` —
  reads the build-time `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK` and the global free
  count. `ensures` (on success) gives `spec_watermark_ok` and keeps
  `free_frames` finite.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::alloc_many_user_frames`
  — loop-allocates `count` user frames into a caller `&mut Vec`, with all-or-
  nothing cleanup. `ensures` gives `len == count` and each frame allocated on
  success, empty vector on error.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::alloc_kernel_frame` —
  like `alloc_user_frame` but yields a `KernelFrame`.
- `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs::PhysMemoryManager::alloc_many_kernel_frames`
  — like `alloc_many_user_frames` plus the contiguity guarantee
  (`kernel_frames_contiguous`) required for kernel stacks.

5. //
6. // `UserFrame` is an RAII owning handle to one reference of a reference-counted
7. // physical user frame, abstracted by the physical address of the frame it owns
8. // (`UserFrame@ : int`, defined by the `View` impl below). `Upool` is a
9. // stateless allocation facade with no caller-observable state, so it has no
10. // `View`.
11. //
12. // All mutable state (which frames are allocated, and per-frame refcounts) lives
13. // in the do-not-modify `FrameAllocView` reached through `phys_view()`
14. // (`mod.spec.rs`). Because `phys_view()` is a zero-argument uninterpreted spec
15. // function (a single fixed value at the current program point), the frame
16. // allocator's effect is expressed as monotone single-state facts over
17. // `phys_view().frames`, exactly like the `frame::*` / `PhysMemoryManager::*`
18. // shim contracts -- there is no `old(phys_view())` to state a before/after
19. // transition against.

22. 
23. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
24. use crate::mm::phys::phys_view;
25. 
26. /// Abstract view of a [`UserFrame`]: the physical address of the frame it owns.
27. ///
28. /// Lets allocator contracts name a returned user frame's address (e.g. "the
29. /// returned frame is now allocated") without exposing any storage detail.
30. impl View for UserFrame {
31.     type V = int;
32. 
33.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
34.         self.addr@
35.     }
36. }
37. 
38. impl UserFrame {
39.     /// A user-frame handle is well-formed iff the frame it names is
40.     /// page-aligned: it denotes a real physical frame, not an arbitrary byte.
41.     ///
42.     /// This is the only abstraction-level fact provable about a handle in
43.     /// isolation. Stronger facts -- "this frame is currently allocated", "its
44.     /// refcount is `n`" -- are properties of `phys_view().frames` keyed by
45.     /// `self@`, not invariants of the handle (a sibling `share`/`drop` changes
46.     /// them without changing this handle), so they are stated in
47.     /// `requires`/`ensures` over `phys_view()` instead.
48.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
49.         self@ % spec_page_size() == 0
50.     }

4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================
7. 
8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("upool.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("upool.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use crate::{
15.     hal::mem::FrameAddress,
16.     mm::phys::frame,
17. };
18. use ::core::mem::ManuallyDrop;
19. use ::sys::error::Error;
20. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
21. use ::vstd::prelude::*;
22. 
23. //==================================================================================================
24. // User Frame
25. //==================================================================================================
26. 
27. ///
28. /// # Description
29. ///
30. /// A type that represents a user frame.
31. ///
32. #[derive(Debug)]
33. #[verus_verify]
34. pub struct UserFrame {
35.     /// Frame address.
36.     addr: FrameAddress,
37. }
38. 
39. #[verus_verify]
40. impl UserFrame {
41.     ///
42.     /// # Description
43.     ///
44.     /// Instantiates a user frame.
45.     ///
46.     /// # Parameters
47.     ///
48.     /// - `addr`: Frame address.
49.     ///
50.     /// # Returns
51.     ///
52.     /// A user frame.
53.     ///
54.     #[verus_spec(ret =>
55.         requires
56.             addr.inv(),
57.         ensures
58.             // `new` merely names an existing frame: the handle's address is `addr`
59.             // and it inherits `addr`'s page-alignment. No allocation and no
60.             // refcount change occur (ownership semantics come from `Drop`/`leak`),
61.             // so `new` says nothing about `phys_view()`.
62.             ret@ == addr@,
63.             ret.inv(),
64.     )]
65.     pub fn new(addr: FrameAddress) -> Self {
66.         Self { addr }
67.     }
68. 
69.     ///
70.     /// # Description
71.     ///
72.     /// Returns the physical address of the target user frame.
73.     ///
74.     /// # Returns
75.     ///
76.     /// The physical address of the target user frame.
77.     ///
78.     #[verus_spec(ret =>
79.         ensures
80.             // Pure getter: returns exactly the address the handle owns.
81.             ret@ == self@,
82.     )]
83.     pub fn address(&self) -> FrameAddress {
84.         self.addr
85.     }
86. 
87.     ///
88.     /// # Description
89.     ///
90.     /// Consumes the user frame without freeing the underlying physical frame.
91.     ///
92.     /// # Returns
93.     ///
94.     /// The frame address.
95.     ///
96.     #[verus_spec(ret =>
97.         ensures
98.             // Consumes the handle and returns its address without releasing the
99.             // reference: `Drop` is suppressed (via `ManuallyDrop`), so the frame
100.             // stays allocated and `phys_view()` is unchanged.
101.             ret@ == self@,
102.     )]
103.     pub fn leak(self) -> FrameAddress {
104.         let this: ManuallyDrop<Self> = ManuallyDrop::new(self);
105.         this.addr
106.     }
107. 
108.     ///
109.     /// # Description
110.     ///
111.     /// Adds a new reference to the underlying physical frame and returns a fresh
112.     /// [`UserFrame`] handle that owns that reference. The two handles share the
113.     /// same physical frame, and the frame is only reclaimed once both handles are
114.     /// dropped.
115.     ///
116.     /// This is the building block for copy-on-write sharing: the parent retains
117.     /// its handle, the child receives the returned handle.
118.     ///
119.     /// # Returns
120.     ///
121.     /// On success, a new [`UserFrame`] that aliases the same physical frame as
122.     /// `self`. On failure, an error is returned.
123.     ///
124.     #[verus_spec(child =>
125.         requires
126.             self.inv(),
127.             phys_view().initialized,
128.             phys_view().inv(),
129.         ensures
130.             phys_view().inv(),
131.             phys_view().initialized,
132.             // On success: a fresh handle aliasing the same physical frame (equal
133.             // view), well-formed, and the frame is still allocated (it has gained
134.             // a reference). On failure: no reference acquired; `self` is untouched.
135.             match child {
136.                 Ok(handle) => {
137.                     &&& handle@ == self@
138.                     &&& handle.inv()
139.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(handle@)
140.                 },
141.                 Err(_) => true,
142.             },
143.     )]
144.     pub fn share(&self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error> {
145.         frame::share(self.addr)?;
146.         Ok(Self { addr: self.addr })
147.     }
148. 
149.     ///
150.     /// # Description
151.     ///
152.     /// Returns the current reference count of the underlying physical frame.
153.     ///
154.     /// # Returns
155.     ///
156.     /// Upon success, the current reference count of the underlying physical frame is returned.
157.     /// Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
158.     ///
159.     #[verus_spec(result =>
160.         requires
161.             self.inv(),
162.             phys_view().initialized,
163.             phys_view().inv(),
164.         ensures
165.             phys_view().inv(),
166.             phys_view().initialized,
167.             // Pure query of the underlying frame's reference count: neither
168.             // consumes `self` nor changes the count. On success the frame is
169.             // allocated and the returned count equals its refcount; on failure the
170.             // frame is not allocated.
171.             match result {
172.                 Ok(count) => {
173.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(self@)
174.                     &&& phys_view().frames.refcounts.contains_key(self@)
175.                     &&& count as int == phys_view().frames.refcounts[self@]
176.                 },
177.                 Err(_) => !phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(self@),
178.             },
179.     )]
180.     pub fn refcount(&self) -> Result<u8, Error> {
181.         frame::refcount(self.addr)
182.     }
183. }
184. 
185. #[verus_verify]
186. impl Drop for UserFrame {
187.     #[verus_spec(
188.         ensures
189.             // Releasing a reference preserves the subsystem invariant (the last
190.             // reference returns the frame to the free pool). The precise refcount
191.             // transition is not expressible: `phys_view()` is a single fixed value
192.             // with no `old(phys_view())` to compare against. Errors are logged, not
193.             // propagated, so `drop` cannot unwind.
194.             phys_view().inv(),
195.         opens_invariants none
196.         no_unwind
197.     )]
198.     fn drop(&mut self) {
199.         if let Err(e) = frame::free(self.addr) {
200.             error!("failed to free user frame: {:?}", e);
201.         }
202.     }
203. }
204. 
205. //==================================================================================================
206. // User Frame Pool
207. //==================================================================================================
208. 
209. ///
210. /// # Description
211. ///
212. /// Thin facade over the module-level [`frame`](super::frame) allocator. Exists as a distinct type
213. /// so user-frame allocation has its own entry point ([`Upool::alloc`] returning [`UserFrame`]).
214. ///
215. #[derive(Debug)]
216. #[verus_verify]
217. pub struct Upool {
218.     /// Private field prevents external construction.
219.     _private: (),
220. }
221. 
222. #[verus_verify]
223. impl Upool {
224.     ///
225.     /// # Description
226.     ///
227.     /// Instantiates a user frame pool.
228.     ///
229.     /// # Returns
230.     ///
231.     /// A user frame pool.
232.     ///
233.     #[verus_verify]
234.     pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
235.         Self { _private: () }
236.     }
237. 
238.     ///
239.     /// # Description
240.     ///
241.     /// Allocates a single user frame from the user frame pool.
242.     ///
243.     /// # Returns
244.     ///
245.     /// Upon success, a user frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
246.     ///
247.     #[verus_spec(result =>
248.         requires
249.             phys_view().initialized,
250.             phys_view().inv(),
251.         ensures
252.             phys_view().inv(),
253.             phys_view().initialized,
254.             // On success: a handle owning a freshly allocated, page-aligned frame
255.             // whose address is now reserved (`allocated_frames`) with a single
256.             // reference. On failure: nothing is reported about the absent frame.
257.             match result {
258.                 Ok(uf) => {
259.                     &&& uf.inv()
260.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(uf@)
261.                     &&& phys_view().frames.refcounts.contains_key(uf@)
262.                     &&& phys_view().frames.refcounts[uf@] == 1
263.                 },
264.                 Err(_) => true,
265.             },
266.     )]
267.     pub fn alloc(&mut self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error> {
268.         let addr: FrameAddress = frame::alloc()?;
269.         Ok(UserFrame::new(addr))
270.     }
271. }

data.deltaContent: I
'm noticing a critical gap between what cal
lers expect from `UserFrame::share` and what the current spec actually guarantees. Callers assume the
refcount increments by one on success and the parent remains untouched on failure, but the spec doesn't explicitly state the refcount increment
—it only describes the postconditions around handle equality and
frame allocation, which doesn't fully capture the reference counting semantics that bugs
.md hints at.
More
importantly, both `share` and `alloc` have `Err(_) => true` in their ensures clauses, which the checklist flags as potentially
tautological. The refcount spec's error arm is meaningful (`!allocated_frames.contains(self@)`), so why can't `
share` say something similar? The honest answer is that `phys_view()` is a single fixed
value with no `old()` to compare against, making "unchanged on error" inexpressible—but this raises
a judgment call about whether `Err(_) => true` is genuinely honest or just sub
sumed by the inability to express state preservation.
The
error paths for alloc and share genuinely can't express anything more
meaningful than `true` given the single-state constraint — alloc fails when no frames exist (
the absent frame has no address to reference), and share can fail even when the frame is
allocated (refcount overflow), so neither can honestly claim a specific prec
ondition. I'll flag this as acceptable-with-justification rather than a blocker, since it al
igns with the established module conventions and reflects the actual limitation. Now
I'm spinning up the verification: running the full test suite to check for cross-module r
egressions, and launching two independent review sub-agents in the background to do static
analysis, spec reconciliation, and caller coverage without running heavy build commands to
avoid contention.

ents concurrently. Sub-agents will do static analysis (no heavy `make` to avoid cargo-lock contention with my central run).

15.     hal::mem::FrameAddress,
16.     mm::phys::frame,
17. };

19. use ::sys::error::Error;
20. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
21. use ::vstd::prelude::*;
22. 
23. //==================================================================================================
24. // User Frame
25. //==================================================================================================
26. 
27. ///
28. /// # Description
29. ///
30. /// A type that represents a user frame.
31. ///
32. #[derive(Debug)]
33. #[verus_verify]
34. pub struct UserFrame {
35.     /// Frame address.
36.     addr: FrameAddress,
37. }
38. 
39. #[verus_verify]
40. impl UserFrame {
41.     ///
42.     /// # Description
43.     ///
44.     /// Instantiates a user frame.
45.     ///
46.     /// # Parameters
47.     ///
48.     /// - `addr`: Frame address.
49.     ///
50.     /// # Returns
51.     ///
52.     /// A user frame.
53.     ///
54.     #[verus_spec(ret =>
55.         requires
56.             addr.inv(),
57.         ensures
58.             // `new` merely names an existing frame: the handle's address is `addr`
59.             // and it inherits `addr`'s page-alignment. No allocation and no
60.             // refcount change occur (ownership semantics come from `Drop`/`leak`),
61.             // so `new` says nothing about `phys_view()`.
62.             ret@ == addr@,
63.             ret.inv(),
64.     )]
65.     pub fn new(addr: FrameAddress) -> Self {
66.         Self { addr }
67.     }
68. 
69.     ///
70.     /// # Description
71.     ///
72.     /// Returns the physical address of the target user frame.
73.     ///
74.     /// # Returns
75.     ///
76.     /// The physical address of the target user frame.
77.     ///
78.     #[verus_spec(ret =>
79.         ensures
80.             // Pure getter: returns exactly the address the handle owns.
81.             ret@ == self@,
82.     )]
83.     pub fn address(&self) -> FrameAddress {
84.         self.addr
85.     }
86. 
87.     ///
88.     /// # Description
89.     ///
90.     /// Consumes the user frame without freeing the underlying physical frame.
91.     ///
92.     /// # Returns
93.     ///
94.     /// The frame address.
95.     ///
96.     #[verus_spec(ret =>
97.         ensures
98.             // Consumes the handle and returns its address without releasing the
99.             // reference: `Drop` is suppressed (via `ManuallyDrop`), so the frame
100.             // stays allocated and `phys_view()` is unchanged.
101.             ret@ == self@,
102.     )]
103.     pub fn leak(self) -> FrameAddress {
104.         let this: ManuallyDrop<Self> = ManuallyDrop::new(self);
105.         this.addr
106.     }
107. 
108.     ///
109.     /// # Description
110.     ///
111.     /// Adds a new reference to the underlying physical frame and returns a fresh
112.     /// [`UserFrame`] handle that owns that reference. The two handles share the
113.     /// same physical frame, and the frame is only reclaimed once both handles are
114.     /// dropped.
115.     ///
116.     /// This is the building block for copy-on-write sharing: the parent retains
117.     /// its handle, the child receives the returned handle.
118.     ///
119.     /// # Returns
120.     ///
121.     /// On success, a new [`UserFrame`] that aliases the same physical frame as
122.     /// `self`. On failure, an error is returned.
123.     ///
124.     #[verus_spec(child =>
125.         requires
126.             self.inv(),
127.             phys_view().initialized,
128.             phys_view().inv(),
129.         ensures
130.             phys_view().inv(),
131.             phys_view().initialized,
132.             // On success: a fresh handle aliasing the same physical frame (equal
133.             // view), well-formed, and the frame is still allocated (it has gained
134.             // a reference). On failure: no reference acquired; `self` is untouched.
135.             match child {
136.                 Ok(handle) => {
137.                     &&& handle@ == self@
138.                     &&& handle.inv()
139.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(handle@)
140.                 },
141.                 Err(_) => true,
142.             },
143.     )]
144.     pub fn share(&self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error> {
145.         frame::share(self.addr)?;
146.         Ok(Self { addr: self.addr })
147.     }
148. 
149.     ///
150.     /// # Description
151.     ///
152.     /// Returns the current reference count of the underlying physical frame.
153.     ///
154.     /// # Returns
155.     ///
156.     /// Upon success, the current reference count of the underlying physical frame is returned.
157.     /// Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
158.     ///
159.     #[verus_spec(result =>
160.         requires
161.             self.inv(),
162.             phys_view().initialized,
163.             phys_view().inv(),
164.         ensures
165.             phys_view().inv(),
166.             phys_view().initialized,
167.             // Pure query of the underlying frame's reference count: neither
168.             // consumes `self` nor changes the count. On success the frame is
169.             // allocated and the returned count equals its refcount; on failure the
170.             // frame is not allocated.
171.             match result {
172.                 Ok(count) => {
173.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(self@)
174.                     &&& phys_view().frames.refcounts.contains_key(self@)
175.                     &&& count as int == phys_view().frames.refcounts[self@]
176.                 },
177.                 Err(_) => !phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(self@),
178.             },
179.     )]
180.     pub fn refcount(&self) -> Result<u8, Error> {
181.         frame::refcount(self.addr)
182.     }
183. }
184. 
185. #[verus_verify]
186. impl Drop for UserFrame {
187.     #[verus_spec(
188.         ensures
189.             // Releasing a reference preserves the subsystem invariant (the last
190.             // reference returns the frame to the free pool). The precise refcount
191.             // transition is not expressible: `phys_view()` is a single fixed value
192.             // with no `old(phys_view())` to compare against. Errors are logged, not
193.             // propagated, so `drop` cannot unwind.
194.             phys_view().inv(),
195.         opens_invariants none
196.         no_unwind
197.     )]
198.     fn drop(&mut self) {
199.         if let Err(e) = frame::free(self.addr) {
200.             error!("failed to free user frame: {:?}", e);
201.         }
202.     }
203. }

209. ///
210. /// # Description
211. ///
212. /// Thin facade over the module-level [`frame`](super::frame) allocator. Exists as a distinct type
213. /// so user-frame allocation has its own entry point ([`Upool::alloc`] returning [`UserFrame`]).
214. ///
215. #[derive(Debug)]
216. #[verus_verify]
217. pub struct Upool {
218.     /// Private field prevents external construction.
219.     _private: (),
220. }
221.

223. impl Upool {
224.     ///
225.     /// # Description
226.     ///
227.     /// Instantiates a user frame pool.
228.     ///
229.     /// # Returns
230.     ///
231.     /// A user frame pool.
232.     ///
233.     #[verus_verify]
234.     pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
235.         Self { _private: () }
236.     }
237. 
238.     ///
239.     /// # Description
240.     ///
241.     /// Allocates a single user frame from the user frame pool.
242.     ///
243.     /// # Returns
244.     ///
245.     /// Upon success, a user frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
246.     ///
247.     #[verus_spec(result =>
248.         requires
249.             phys_view().initialized,
250.             phys_view().inv(),
251.         ensures
252.             phys_view().inv(),
253.             phys_view().initialized,
254.             // On success: a handle owning a freshly allocated, page-aligned frame
255.             // whose address is now reserved (`allocated_frames`) with a single
256.             // reference. On failure: nothing is reported about the absent frame.
257.             match result {
258.                 Ok(uf) => {
259.                     &&& uf.inv()
260.                     &&& phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(uf@)
261.                     &&& phys_view().frames.refcounts.contains_key(uf@)
262.                     &&& phys_view().frames.refcounts[uf@] == 1
263.                 },
264.                 Err(_) => true,
265.             },
266.     )]

268.         let addr: FrameAddress = frame::alloc()?;

1. # Caller Analysis: `mm::phys::upool`
2. 
3. ## Script Output
4. See: `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-upool/find_callers_output.md`
5. (generated by `scripts/find_callers_lsp.py`)
6. 
7. - Crate: `kernel` (intra-crate analysis only; no external crate dependents).
8. - 8 exec functions in scope, all `pub`/`pub(super)`/trait-pub, 0 private.
9. - 2 public types: `UserFrame` (19 refs), `Upool` (6 refs).
10. 
11. ## Module Overview
12. 
13. `upool.rs` provides two types:
14. 
15. - **`UserFrame`** — an *owning handle* to a single reference-counted physical
16.   user frame. It stores only a `FrameAddress`. All real work is delegated to the
17.   module-level `frame` allocator:
18.   - `share`  → `frame::share`  (increment refcount)
19.   - `refcount` → `frame::refcount` (query refcount)
20.   - `drop`   → `frame::free`    (decrement / release on scope exit)
21. - **`Upool`** — a zero-sized facade (`_private: ()`) that is the dedicated entry
22.   point for user-frame allocation (`alloc` → `frame::alloc`).
23. 
24. All callers live under `src/kernel/src/mm/` (`virt/vmem.rs`, `virt/manager.rs`,
25. `phys/manager.rs`, `phys/mod.rs`, `elf.rs`).
26. 
27. ## Trait Obligations
28. 
29. - **Trait: `Drop for UserFrame`** — expected semantics: when a live `UserFrame`
30.   goes out of scope, it **releases exactly one reference** to its physical frame
31.   (`frame::free`), freeing the frame only when the last reference drops. Errors
32.   are logged, not propagated. Callers rely on this for automatic refcount
33.   release and for CoW reference dropping (`drop(UserFrame::new(old_frame))` at
34.   `vmem.rs:895`) and error-path rollback (a failed `map` drops the unmapped
35.   handle, releasing the freshly `share`d reference).
36. - **Trait: `View for UserFrame`** (already present in the file) — `view() : int`
37.   is the physical address of the owned frame (`self.addr@`). Upstream specs
38.   already depend on this: `PhysMemoryManager::alloc_user_frame` ensures
39.   `phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)` and
40.   `frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0` over the returned `UserFrame`.
41. 
42. ## Caller Expectations
43. 
44. ### `UserFrame::new(addr) -> Self`
45. Callers: `vmem.rs:869,895,1522`, `manager.rs:349`, internal `Upool::alloc`.
46. - Callers assume: produces a handle whose `view() == addr@`, treated as *owning*
47.   one reference to the frame at `addr`. Used to (a) wrap an already-owned address
48.   so a method (`share`/`refcount`) can be called on it via `ManuallyDrop`
49.   (869, 349), (b) reconstruct a droppable handle to release a reference
50.   (`drop(UserFrame::new(old_frame))`, 895), and (c) hand a frame back to the
51.   caller after `unmap` (1522).
52. - Callers don't care about: how the address is stored. Only that `new` performs
53.   **no allocation and no refcount change** — it merely names an existing frame;
54.   ownership semantics come solely from `Drop`/`leak`.
55. 
56. ### `UserFrame::address(&self) -> FrameAddress`
57. Callers: `vmem.rs:361,882,887`.
58. - Callers assume: a pure, side-effect-free getter that returns the exact
59.   `FrameAddress` the handle owns (`view()` as a concrete address). Used to feed
60.   `page_table.map(...)` (361), compute a memcpy destination (882), and repoint a
61.   PTE (887). Must not consume or mutate `self`.
62. - Callers don't care about: any internal representation; only `address()@ == self@`.
63. 
64. ### `UserFrame::leak(self) -> FrameAddress`
65. Callers: `vmem.rs:368,891`.
66. - Callers assume: consumes the handle **without** decrementing the refcount /
67.   freeing the frame (suppresses `Drop`), returning the address. Used after
68.   ownership of the frame has been transferred to a page table, so the frame must
69.   **remain allocated**.
70. - Callers don't care about the return value at 368/891 (`uframe.leak();`,
71.   `let _ = new_frame.leak();`) — they only need the no-free guarantee.
72. 
73. ### `UserFrame::share(&self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error>`
74. Caller: `manager.rs:350` (`child_handle = parent_handle.share()?`).
75. - Callers assume on success: a **new** `UserFrame` aliasing the same physical
76.   frame (returned `view() == self@`) with the refcount **incremented by one**, so
77.   the parent and child each independently own a reference (CoW building block).
78. - Callers assume on failure: **no state change** — no reference acquired, parent
79.   untouched (the parent is held in `ManuallyDrop` precisely so a `share` error
80.   cannot spuriously decrement it).
81. - Callers don't care about: how sharing is implemented in the `frame` allocator.
82. 
83. ### `UserFrame::refcount(&self) -> Result<u8, Error>`
84. Caller: `vmem.rs:870` (`if probe.refcount()? == 1`).
85. - Callers assume: a pure query returning the current refcount of the underlying
86.   frame; does not consume or mutate `self` and does not change the count. Used to
87.   detect the "last reference" CoW fast path. (Caller wraps the probe in
88.   `ManuallyDrop` so the query handle won't free the frame.)
89. - Callers don't care about: anything beyond the numeric count.
90.

 # Caller Analysis: `mm::phys::upool`
 
 ## Script Output
 See: `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-upool/find_callers_output.md`
 (generated by `scripts/find_callers_lsp.py`)
 
 - Crate: `kernel` (intra-crate analysis only; no external crate dependents).
 - 8 exec functions in scope, all `pub`/`pub(super)`/trait-pub, 0 private.
 - 2 public types: `UserFrame` (19 refs), `Upool` (6 refs).
 
 ## Module Overview
 
 `upool.rs` provides two types:
 
 - **`UserFrame`** — an *owning handle* to a single reference-counted physical
   user frame. It stores only a `FrameAddress`. All real work is delegated to the
   module-level `frame` allocator:
   - `share`  → `frame::share`  (increment refcount)
   - `refcount` → `frame::refcount` (query refcount)
   - `drop`   → `frame::free`    (decrement / release on scope exit)
 - **`Upool`** — a zero-sized facade (`_private: ()`) that is the dedicated entry
   point for user-frame allocation (`alloc` → `frame::alloc`).
 
 All callers live under `src/kernel/src/mm/` (`virt/vmem.rs`, `virt/manager.rs`,
 `phys/manager.rs`, `phys/mod.rs`, `elf.rs`).
 
 ## Trait Obligations
 
 - **Trait: `Drop for UserFrame`** — expected semantics: when a live `UserFrame`
   goes out of scope, it **releases exactly one reference** to its physical frame
   (`frame::free`), freeing the frame only when the last reference drops. Errors
   are logged, not propagated. Callers rely on this for automatic refcount
   release and for CoW reference dropping (`drop(UserFrame::new(old_frame))` at
   `vmem.rs:895`) and error-path rollback (a failed `map` drops the unmapped
   handle, releasing the freshly `share`d reference).
 - **Trait: `View for UserFrame`** (already present in the file) — `view() : int`
   is the physical address of the owned frame (`self.addr@`). Upstream specs
   already depend on this: `PhysMemoryManager::alloc_user_frame` ensures
   `phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(frame@)` and
   `frame@ % spec_page_size() == 0` over the returned `UserFrame`.
 
 ## Caller Expectations
 
 ### `UserFrame::new(addr) -> Self`
 Callers: `vmem.rs:869,895,1522`, `manager.rs:349`, internal `Upool::alloc`.
 - Callers assume: produces a handle whose `view() == addr@`, treated as *owning*
   one reference to the frame at `addr`. Used to (a) wrap an already-owned address
   so a method (`share`/`refcount`) can be called on it via `ManuallyDrop`
   (869, 349), (b) reconstruct a droppable handle to release a reference
   (`drop(UserFrame::new(old_frame))`, 895), and (c) hand a frame back to the
   caller after `unmap` (1522).
 - Callers don't care about: how the address is stored. Only that `new` performs
   **no allocation and no refcount change** — it merely names an existing frame;
   ownership semantics come solely from `Drop`/`leak`.
 
 ### `UserFrame::address(&self) -> FrameAddress`
 Callers: `vmem.rs:361,882,887`.
 - Callers assume: a pure, side-effect-free getter that returns the exact
   `FrameAddress` the handle owns (`view()` as a concrete address). Used to feed
   `page_table.map(...)` (361), compute a memcpy destination (882), and repoint a
   PTE (887). Must not consume or mutate `self`.
 - Callers don't care about: any internal representation; only `address()@ == self@`.
 
 ### `UserFrame::leak(self) -> FrameAddress`
 Callers: `vmem.rs:368,891`.
 - Callers assume: consumes the handle **without** decrementing the refcount /
   freeing the frame (suppresses `Drop`), returning the address. Used after
   ownership of the frame has been transferred to a page table, so the frame must
   **remain allocated**.
 - Callers don't care about the return value at 368/891 (`uframe.leak();`,
   `let _ = new_frame.leak();`) — they only need the no-free guarantee.
 
 ### `UserFrame::share(&self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error>`
 Caller: `manager.rs:350` (`child_handle = parent_handle.share()?`).
 - Callers assume on success: a **new** `UserFrame` aliasing the same physical
   frame (returned `view() == self@`) with the refcount **incremented by one**, so
   the parent and child each independently own a reference (CoW building block).
 - Callers assume on failure: **no state change** — no reference acquired, parent
   untouched (the parent is held in `ManuallyDrop` precisely so a `share` error
   cannot spuriously decrement it).
 - Callers don't care about: how sharing is implemented in the `frame` allocator.
 
 ### `UserFrame::refcount(&self) -> Result<u8, Error>`
 Caller: `vmem.rs:870` (`if probe.refcount()? == 1`).
 - Callers assume: a pure query returning the current refcount of the underlying
   frame; does not consume or mutate `self` and does not change the count. Used to
   detect the "last reference" CoW fast path. (Caller wraps the probe in
   `ManuallyDrop` so the query handle won't free the frame.)
 - Callers don't care about: anything beyond the numeric count.
 
 ### `UserFrame::drop(&mut self)` (implicit)
 Callers: compiler-inserted at scope exit; explicit `drop(...)` at `vmem.rs:895`;
 error rollback paths in `map`/`mark_cow`.
 - See Trait Obligations. Releases exactly one reference; frees only on the last.
 
 ### `Upool::new() -> Self` `[pub(super)]`
 Caller: `phys/mod.rs:197` (then `PhysMemoryManager::init(upool)`).
 - Callers assume: constructs the allocation facade with **no allocation or
   global-state mutation**; the value is immediately moved into the singleton.
 - Callers don't care about: the `_private: ()` field (exists only to block
   external construction). Marked `external_body` (allowed — trivial constructor).
 
 ### `Upool::alloc(&mut self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error>`
 Callers: `phys/manager.rs:269` (`alloc_user_frame`), `:222` (`alloc_many_user_frames` loop).
 - Callers assume on success: returns a `UserFrame` owning a **freshly allocated,
   page-aligned** physical frame (`view()` == its address; that address is now in
   `allocated_frames`). The returned handle carries one reference and will free it
   on drop. The watermark gate is enforced by the *caller*
   (`check_user_watermark`), not by `alloc` itself.
 - Callers assume on failure: **nothing allocated**, no leaked frame.
 - Callers don't care about: that `alloc` just forwards to `frame::alloc` and
   wraps the result in `UserFrame::new`.
 
 ## Abstract Resource
 
 `UserFrame` is an **RAII owning handle to one reference of a reference-counted
 physical user frame**, identified abstractly by its physical address
 (`view() : int`). `Upool` is the stateless allocation entry point that mints such
 handles. The module manages *ownership of frame references*, not frame storage —
 the actual refcount/bitmap state lives in the `frame` allocator.
 
 ## Key Invariants (caller perspective)
 
 - A `UserFrame`'s `view()` is the physical address of the frame it owns and is
   **stable**: `address()@ == self@`, and `new(a)@ == a@`.
 - A live `UserFrame` owns exactly **one** reference to its frame.
   - `Drop` releases exactly one reference (frees on the last).
   - `leak` discards the handle **without** releasing its reference (frame stays
     allocated).
   - `share` **adds** one reference and yields an aliasing handle with equal view.
   - `refcount`/`address` are pure: they neither consume the handle nor change the
     refcount.
 - `Upool::alloc` (and thus `alloc_user_frame`) yields a handle to a newly
   allocated, **page-aligned** frame on success; on error no frame is allocated.
 - Construction (`Upool::new`, `UserFrame::new`) performs no allocation and no
   refcount change.
 
 ## Pre-existing Specs (from upstream verification)
 
 - Source files `upool.spec.rs` / `upool.proof.rs` are empty stubs
   (`verus! { }`). There are **no** `#[verus_spec]` annotations on any of the 8
   target functions in `upool.rs`.
 - A `View for UserFrame` impl **already exists** in `upool.rs`
   (`type V = int; view() = self.addr@`). It is *not* in the do-not-modify list
   (that list covers the `frame` allocator's `Inner`/`FrameAllocView`), but it is
   already consumed by `phys/manager.rs` specs (`alloc_user_frame`,
   `alloc_many_user_frames`) which reference `frame@` and
   `final(frames)@[i]@`. Treat this `int`-address View as the established,
   caller-validated abstraction.
 
 ### Assessment
 - Coverage: **none** at the `upool` function level (no specs yet on the 8
   targets) — only the `View` type pre-exists.
 - View design: **caller-abstract** — `int` physical address exposes exactly what
   every caller needs (mapping, memcpy, PTE repointing, allocation-set membership,
   alignment) and hides all storage/refcount detail. No bias toward a single
   caller.

1. # View Design: `mm::phys::upool`
2. 
3. ## Abstract Resource
4. 
5. `upool` exposes two caller-facing types:
6. 
7. - **`UserFrame`** — an RAII *owning handle* to **one reference** of a
8.   reference-counted physical user frame. To a caller, a `UserFrame` is fully
9.   described by a single piece of abstract state: **the physical address of the
10.   frame it owns** (`int`). It carries no other observable state — the refcount
11.   and allocated/free status of that frame live in the *global* frame-allocator
12.   state (`phys_view().frames : FrameAllocView`), not inside the handle.
13. 
14. - **`Upool`** — a zero-sized (`_private: ()`) allocation *facade*. It owns **no
15.   abstract state at all**; it is merely the typed entry point that mints
16.   `UserFrame`s by forwarding to the global `frame` allocator. Its `&mut self`
17.   receiver is vestigial: the only state `alloc` mutates is the global allocator,
18.   not the `Upool` value.
19. 
20. The module therefore manages **ownership of frame references**, not frame
21. storage. The authoritative, mutable state (which frames are allocated, and each
22. frame's refcount) is the pre-existing, do-not-modify `FrameAllocView` reached
23. through `phys_view()`.
24. 
25. ---
26. 
27. ## View Struct
28. 
29. ### `UserFrame` — keep the existing `int` view (recommended, unchanged)
30. 
31. ```rust
32. // Already present in upool.rs — endorsed by this design, do not change.
33. impl View for UserFrame {
34.     type V = int;
35. 
36.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
37.         self.addr@           // physical address of the owned frame
38.     }
39. }
40. ```
41. 
42. `UserFrame@ : int` is the **complete** abstract state of the handle. The handle's
43. identity *is* the physical address of the frame it names; everything else a
44. caller cares about (is it allocated? what is its refcount?) is a property of the
45. *global allocator at that address*, queried as `phys_view().frames` keyed by
46. `self@`.
47. 
48. `view()` stays `closed`: callers reference `frame@` (already done by
49. `PhysMemoryManager::alloc_user_frame` / `alloc_many_user_frames`), but the fact
50. that it is stored as a `FrameAddress` newtype is hidden.
51. 
52. ### `Upool` — no `View` (recommended)
53. 
54. `Upool` has no caller-observable state, so it gets **no `View` impl**. Adding one
55. would only be able to map to unit, which carries no information and would never
56. appear in a useful spec. `Upool::alloc`/`Upool::new` contracts are written
57. entirely against `phys_view()` (see Spec Transitions), so a `Upool` view is dead
58. weight. (If the verifier later requires *some* view for `&mut self`, a trivial
59. `type V = (); view() = ()` is acceptable, but it is intentionally omitted here.)
60. 
61. ---
62. 
63. ## Well-formedness Invariant
64. 
65. ```rust
66. impl UserFrame {
67.     /// A user-frame handle is well-formed iff the frame it names is
68.     /// page-aligned (it denotes a real physical frame, not an arbitrary byte).
69.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
70.         self@ % spec_page_size() == 0
71.     }
72. }
73. ```
74. 
75. This delegates to the alignment property that `FrameAddress::inv()` already
76. guarantees (`self@ % spec_page_size() == 0`). It is the only abstraction-level
77. constraint a caller can state about a `UserFrame` *in isolation*: a handle names
78. a page frame. Stronger facts — "this frame is currently allocated", "its refcount
79. is `n`" — are **not** invariants of the handle; they are properties of
80. `phys_view().frames` and must be expressed there, because `leak`/`drop`/`share`
81. change them without changing the handle.
82. 
83. No `inv()` is defined for `Upool` (no state to constrain).
84. 
85. ---
86. 
87. ## Spec Transition Functions
88. 
89. `UserFrame`'s own view is **immutable** — no operation changes `self@` (the
90. address an owned handle names never changes). Therefore the meaningful "state
91. transitions" of this module are transitions of the **global allocator view**
92. `phys_view().frames : FrameAllocView`, reached through `phys_view()`.
93. 
94. `FrameAllocView` is on the do-not-modify list, so these transitions are **not**
95. new methods on it. They are expressed in `upool.spec.rs` either inline in
96. `ensures` clauses over the existing fields (`allocated_frames`, `free_frames`,
97. `refcounts`) or, for readability, as standalone helper spec fns that take and
98. return a `FrameAllocView`. Proposed helpers:
99. 
100. ```rust
101. // in upool.spec.rs — operate on (do not modify) FrameAllocView.
102. 
103. /// `share`: add one reference to an already-allocated frame.
104. pub open spec fn spec_add_ref(v: FrameAllocView, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
105.     FrameAllocView {
106.         refcounts: v.refcounts.insert(addr, v.refcounts[addr] + 1),
107.         ..v
108.     }
109. }
110. 
111. /// `drop` of a non-last reference: drop one reference, frame stays allocated.
112. pub open spec fn spec_drop_ref(v: FrameAllocView, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
113.     FrameAllocView {
114.         refcounts: v.refcounts.insert(addr, v.refcounts[addr] - 1),
115.         ..v
116.     }
117. }
118. 
119. /// `drop` of the last reference: refcount hits 0, frame returns to free.
120. pub open spec fn spec_release(v: FrameAllocView, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
121.     FrameAllocView {
122.         allocated_frames: v.allocated_frames.remove(addr),
123.         free_frames:      v.free_frames.insert(addr),
124.         refcounts:        v.refcounts.remove(addr),
125.     }
126. }
127. ```
128. 
129. Per-function mapping (target functions in scope):
130. 
131. | Function | Effect on `UserFrame@` | Effect on `phys_view().frames` |
132. |---|---|---|
133. | `UserFrame::new(addr)` | `ret@ == addr@` | **none** — names an existing frame; no alloc, no refcount change |
134. | `UserFrame::address(&self)` | pure; `ret@ == self@` | **none** (pure getter) |
135. | `UserFrame::leak(self)` | `ret@ == self@` | **none** — suppresses `Drop`; frame stays allocated, refcount unchanged |
136. | `UserFrame::refcount(&self)` | pure | **none**; on `Ok(c)`, `c == old.refcounts[self@]` |
137. | `UserFrame::share(&self)` | `ret.ok@ == self@` | `Ok`: `final == spec_add_ref(old, self@)`; `Err`: `final == old` |
138. | `UserFrame::drop(&mut self)` | n/a (consumed) | non-last ref: `spec_drop_ref`; last ref: `spec_release`; keyed on `self@` |
139. | `Upool::new()` | n/a | **none** — no allocation, no global mutation |
140. | `Upool::alloc(&mut self)` | `Ok(uf)`: fresh frame, `uf@ % page == 0`, `uf@ ∈ final.allocated_frames`, `final.refcounts[uf@] == 1` | `Err`: `final == old` (nothing allocated) |
141. 
142. Notes:
143. - `alloc` chooses *some* free frame; its postcondition is best stated as
144.   membership (`uf@ ∈ final.allocated_frames`, `uf@ ∉ old.allocated_frames`,
145.   `final.refcounts[uf@] == 1`) rather than a deterministic transition, because
146.   the choice of frame is an allocator detail the caller cannot predict.
147. - `share`/`refcount` require `self@ ∈ old.allocated_frames` (the frame must be
148.   live to add a reference to / query it) — this matches `frame::share`/
149.   `frame::refcount` preconditions and is a property of `phys_view()`, not of the
150.   handle.
151. - The "no-change" rows (`new`, `address`, `leak`, `refcount`, `Upool::new`,
152.   and the `Err` arms) are real, required frame conditions: `final(phys_view) ==
153.   old(phys_view)`. They are what makes `leak`'s no-free guarantee and `share`'s
154.   failure-atomicity provable.
155. 
156. ---
157. 
158. ## Design Rationale
159. 
160. ### `UserFrame@ : int` (physical address) — the single field
161. 
162. - **Substitution test**: *passes.* If `UserFrame` were re-implemented to store a
163.   frame *number*, a raw `usize`, a `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>`, or anything
164.   else, the abstract identity callers reason about is still "the physical address
165.   of the owned frame." Every caller (page-table `map`, memcpy destination, PTE
166.   repointing, allocation-set membership, alignment checks) uses exactly this and
167.   nothing about the storage form.
168. - **Caller-only**: every cited caller already uses `frame@`/`view()` as the
169.   address; none depends on representation.
170. - **Complete**: combined with `phys_view().frames`, the address is sufficient to
171.   state every caller-observable property — allocation (`allocated_frames.contains(self@)`),
172.   refcount (`refcounts[self@]`), alignment (`self@ % page == 0`).
173. - **Minimal**: one field, used by every spec.
174. - **WHAT not HOW**: it names a frame; it does not describe how the handle stores
175.   or releases it.
176. 
177. ### Why refcount / allocation status are **not** fields of `UserFrame`'s view
178. 
179. This is the crux of the design and the main substitution-test outcome.
180. 
181. A tempting alternative is to make `UserFrame@` a record like
182. `{ addr: int, refcount: int }` or `{ addr: int, live: bool }`. **Rejected**:
183. 
184. - A handle does not *own* the refcount; the refcount is shared mutable state of
185.   the global allocator. `share` on a sibling handle, or `drop` of an aliasing
186.   handle, changes the count of *this* frame without touching *this* handle — so a
187.   refcount field would instantly go stale and could never satisfy a frame
188.   condition. The count is correctly modeled as `phys_view().frames.refcounts[self@]`.
189. - It fails the substitution test in the other direction: it would bake the
190.   refcounting *strategy* into the handle's abstraction, even though refcounting
191.   is an allocator implementation choice (a different implementation could use a
192.   different ownership-tracking scheme while keeping the same `UserFrame` API).
193. 
194. So the handle's view stays a pure identity (`int`), and all mutation is routed
195. through the pre-existing, do-not-modify `FrameAllocView`. This keeps the two
196. abstraction boundaries clean: **`UserFrame@` = *which* frame; `phys_view()` =
197. *its* state.**
198. 
199. ### `Upool` has no view
200. 
201. `Upool` is a zero-sized facade. Its abstract state is empty: `new` allocates
202. nothing and mutates no global state; `alloc` mutates only the global allocator.
203. A view could only be unit and would never appear in a spec, so none is defined.
204. This also keeps `Upool::alloc`'s contract honest — it speaks about
205. `phys_view()`, the state it actually changes.
206. 
207. ### `inv()` = page-alignment only
208. 
209. The single well-formedness fact provable about a handle alone is that it names a
210. page-aligned frame. Everything else is conditional on global state and belongs in
211. `ensures`/`requires` over `phys_view()`. Keeping `inv()` minimal avoids coupling
212. the handle to allocator state it doesn't own.
213. 
214. ---
215. 
216. ## Rejected Alternatives
217. 
218. | Candidate | Why rejected |
219. |---|---|
220. | `UserFrame@ = { addr, refcount }` | Refcount is shared global state, not handle state; goes stale under sibling `share`/`drop`; fails substitution (bakes in refcounting strategy). Model as `phys_view().frames.refcounts[self@]`. |
221. | `UserFrame@ = { addr, live: bool }` | "Allocated?" is a property of the global allocator at `self@`, not of the handle; a leaked vs. dropped handle both stop existing yet leave the frame in opposite states. Use `phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(self@)`. |
222. | `UserFrame@` stores `FrameAddress`/`PageAligned<…>`/frame-number | Representation leak; fails substitution. The caller-visible abstraction is the `int` address; keep `view()` `closed`. |
223. | `Upool@ = FrameAllocView` (mirror the allocator) | `Upool` does not own the allocator; it forwards to the global singleton. Duplicating allocator state in `Upool`'s view would create two sources of truth. Reference `phys_view()` instead. |
224. | `Upool@ = ()` (explicit unit view) | Harmless but pure dead weight — never used by any spec. Omit unless the verifier forces a view for `&mut self`. |
225. | New transition methods on `FrameAllocView` (`spec_add_ref`, …) added to `mod.spec.rs` | `FrameAllocView` is do-not-modify. Define the helper spec fns in `upool.spec.rs` taking/returning `FrameAllocView`, or inline the field updates in `ensures`. |
226. | Adding `inv()` clauses about allocation/refcount to `UserFrame` | Those facts are not invariants of the handle (they change without the handle changing). Keep `inv()` to alignment; state the rest in `requires`/`ensures` over `phys_view()`. |
227. 
228. ---
229. 
230. ## Quality Review
231. 
232. | Criterion | Result |
233. |---|---|
234. | **Substitution** | `int` address survives any storage rewrite; rejected fields explicitly fail it. ✅ |
235. | **Caller-only** | Address is the only thing callers use; refcount/allocation come from the already-public `phys_view()`. ✅ |
236. | **Complete** | Address + `phys_view().frames` expresses every caller concept (map, memcpy, PTE, membership, alignment, refcount, share atomicity). ✅ |
237. | **Minimal** | One field for `UserFrame`; zero for `Upool`; every field used in specs. ✅ |
238. | **No code-as-spec** | View states *which* frame is owned; transitions are declarative set/map updates on `FrameAllocView`, not a refcount algorithm. ✅ |
239.

 | `UserFrame::new(addr)` | `ret@ == addr@` | **none** — names an existing frame; no alloc, no refcount change |
 | `UserFrame::address(&self)` | pure; `ret@ == self@` | **none** (pure getter) |
 | `UserFrame::leak(self)` | `ret@ == self@` | **none** — suppresses `Drop`; frame stays allocated, refcount unchanged |
 | `UserFrame::refcount(&self)` | pure | **none**; on `Ok(c)`, `c == old.refcounts[self@]` |
 | `UserFrame::share(&self)` | `ret.ok@ == self@` | `Ok`: `final == spec_add_ref(old, self@)`; `Err`: `final == old` |
 | `UserFrame::drop(&mut self)` | n/a (consumed) | non-last ref: `spec_drop_ref`; last ref: `spec_release`; keyed on `self@` |
 | `Upool::new()` | n/a | **none** — no allocation, no global mutation |
 | `Upool::alloc(&mut self)` | `Ok(uf)`: fresh frame, `uf@ % page == 0`, `uf@ ∈ final.allocated_frames`, `final.refcounts[uf@] == 1` | `Err`: `final == old` (nothing allocated) |
 
 Notes:
 - `alloc` chooses *some* free frame; its postcondition is best stated as
   membership (`uf@ ∈ final.allocated_frames`, `uf@ ∉ old.allocated_frames`,
   `final.refcounts[uf@] == 1`) rather than a deterministic transition, because
   the choice of frame is an allocator detail the caller cannot predict.
 - `share`/`refcount` require `self@ ∈ old.allocated_frames` (the frame must be
   live to add a reference to / query it) — this matches `frame::share`/
   `frame::refcount` preconditions and is a property of `phys_view()`, not of the
   handle.
 - The "no-change" rows (`new`, `address`, `leak`, `refcount`, `Upool::new`,
   and the `Err` arms) are real, required frame conditions: `final(phys_view) ==
   old(phys_view)`. They are what makes `leak`'s no-free guarantee and `share`'s
   failure-atomicity provable.
 
 ---
 
 ## Design Rationale
 
 ### `UserFrame@ : int` (physical address) — the single field
 
 - **Substitution test**: *passes.* If `UserFrame` were re-implemented to store a
   frame *number*, a raw `usize`, a `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>`, or anything
   else, the abstract identity callers reason about is still "the physical address
   of the owned frame." Every caller (page-table `map`, memcpy destination, PTE
   repointing, allocation-set membership, alignment checks) uses exactly this and
   nothing about the storage form.
 - **Caller-only**: every cited caller already uses `frame@`/`view()` as the
   address; none depends on representation.
 - **Complete**: combined with `phys_view().frames`, the address is sufficient to
   state every caller-observable property — allocation (`allocated_frames.contains(self@)`),
   refcount (`refcounts[self@]`), alignment (`self@ % page == 0`).
 - **Minimal**: one field, used by every spec.
 - **WHAT not HOW**: it names a frame; it does not describe how the handle stores
   or releases it.
 
 ### Why refcount / allocation status are **not** fields of `UserFrame`'s view
 
 This is the crux of the design and the main substitution-test outcome.
 
 A tempting alternative is to make `UserFrame@` a record like
 `{ addr: int, refcount: int }` or `{ addr: int, live: bool }`. **Rejected**:
 
 - A handle does not *own* the refcount; the refcount is shared mutable state of
   the global allocator. `share` on a sibling handle, or `drop` of an aliasing
   handle, changes the count of *this* frame without touching *this* handle — so a
   refcount field would instantly go stale and could never satisfy a frame
   condition. The count is correctly modeled as `phys_view().frames.refcounts[self@]`.
 - It fails the substitution test in the other direction: it would bake the
   refcounting *strategy* into the handle's abstraction, even though refcounting
   is an allocator implementation choice (a different implementation could use a
   different ownership-tracking scheme while keeping the same `UserFrame` API).
 
 So the handle's view stays a pure identity (`int`), and all mutation is routed
 through the pre-existing, do-not-modify `FrameAllocView`. This keeps the two
 abstraction boundaries clean: **`UserFrame@` = *which* frame; `phys_view()` =
 *its* state.**
 
 ### `Upool` has no view
 
 `Upool` is a zero-sized facade. Its abstract state is empty: `new` allocates
 nothing and mutates no global state; `alloc` mutates only the global allocator.
 A view could only be unit and would never appear in a spec, so none is defined.
 This also keeps `Upool::alloc`'s contract honest — it speaks about
 `phys_view()`, the state it actually changes.
 
 ### `inv()` = page-alignment only
 
 The single well-formedness fact provable about a handle alone is that it names a
 page-aligned frame. Everything else is conditional on global state and belongs in
 `ensures`/`requires` over `phys_view()`. Keeping `inv()` minimal avoids coupling
 the handle to allocator state it doesn't own.
 
 ---
 
 ## Rejected Alternatives
 
 | Candidate | Why rejected |
 |---|---|
 | `UserFrame@ = { addr, refcount }` | Refcount is shared global state, not handle state; goes stale under sibling `share`/`drop`; fails substitution (bakes in refcounting strategy). Model as `phys_view().frames.refcounts[self@]`. |
 | `UserFrame@ = { addr, live: bool }` | "Allocated?" is a property of the global allocator at `self@`, not of the handle; a leaked vs. dropped handle both stop existing yet leave the frame in opposite states. Use `phys_view().frames.allocated_frames.contains(self@)`. |
 | `UserFrame@` stores `FrameAddress`/`PageAligned<…>`/frame-number | Representation leak; fails substitution. The caller-visible abstraction is the `int` address; keep `view()` `closed`. |
 | `Upool@ = FrameAllocView` (mirror the allocator) | `Upool` does not own the allocator; it forwards to the global singleton. Duplicating allocator state in `Upool`'s view would create two sources of truth. Reference `phys_view()` instead. |
 | `Upool@ = ()` (explicit unit view) | Harmless but pure dead weight — never used by any spec. Omit unless the verifier forces a view for `&mut self`. |
 | New transition methods on `FrameAllocView` (`spec_add_ref`, …) added to `mod.spec.rs` | `FrameAllocView` is do-not-modify. Define the helper spec fns in `upool.spec.rs` taking/returning `FrameAllocView`, or inline the field updates in `ensures`. |
 | Adding `inv()` clauses about allocation/refcount to `UserFrame` | Those facts are not invariants of the handle (they change without the handle changing). Keep `inv()` to alignment; state the rest in `requires`/`ensures` over `phys_view()`. |
 
 ---
 
 ## Quality Review
 
 | Criterion | Result |
 |---|---|
 | **Substitution** | `int` address survives any storage rewrite; rejected fields explicitly fail it. ✅ |
 | **Caller-only** | Address is the only thing callers use; refcount/allocation come from the already-public `phys_view()`. ✅ |
 | **Complete** | Address + `phys_view().frames` expresses every caller concept (map, memcpy, PTE, membership, alignment, refcount, share atomicity). ✅ |
 | **Minimal** | One field for `UserFrame`; zero for `Upool`; every field used in specs. ✅ |
 | **No code-as-spec** | View states *which* frame is owned; transitions are declarative set/map updates on `FrameAllocView`, not a refcount algorithm. ✅ |
